hypothesis: The owner-reported live scores of ~91 hash-identified rasters are noisy measurements of the hidden new-fault set; fitting lambda(x)=exp(theta.phi(x)) so that the official DTI formula in expectation reproduces them yields a truth intensity that a greedy DTI emission can exploit.
mechanism: E[TP_w] is linear in lambda (sum over truth cells of the max-kernel coverage), so each live score constrains theta; basis = distance-to-catalogue bands, 5 km catalogue density, 13 terrain/geophysics ranks, and an HGB catalogue-analogue probability + crest; emission = shared emit.greedy_allocate.
non_fault_mimic: Erosional/lithologic topographic lineaments (resistant ridges, strath terraces, drainage-parallel scarps) that look like mapped faults to the catalogue-analogue ML term and to the det_elev line responses; also the model can absorb owner-pipeline artefacts (e.g. the H19 family's ranking) rather than geology because the scores come from one family of submitters.

holdout.caveat: Catalogue hide-and-recover truth lives inside densely mapped districts; the live-score fit says new faults avoid them (theta[cat_density_5km] < 0), and the incumbent-recipe control descends from a field trained on the FULL catalogue (leak in its favour). The gate is applied literally anyway.
